```xml
<robot name="cabinet_one_door">
  <!-- Dimensions (meters) -->
  <!-- Cabinet overall: width 0.75 (X), height 1.02 (Z), depth 0.41 (Y, positive toward back; front is -Y) -->
  <!-- Origin: floor under middle of object -->
  <!-- Cabinet spans:
       X: [-0.375, +0.375]
       Y: [-0.205, +0.205]
       Z: [0, +1.02]
  -->

  <!-- Links -->

  <link name="base">
    <inertial>
      <origin xyz="0 0 0.51" rpy="0 0 0"/>
      <!-- Approximate steel/wood body mass -->
      <mass value="20.0"/>
      <!-- Box inertia about COM -->
      <inertia ixx="0.140" iyy="0.140" izz="0.031"/>
    </inertial>
    <visual>
      <origin xyz="0 0 0.51" rpy="0 0 0"/>
      <geometry>
        <box size="0.75 0.41 1.02"/>
      </geometry>
      <material name="body_color">
        <color rgba="0.70 0.52 0.32 1"/>
      </material>
    </visual>
    <collision>
      <origin xyz="0 0 0.51" rpy="0 0 0"/>
      <geometry>
        <box size="0.75 0.41 1.02"/>
      </geometry>
    </collision>
  </link>

  <!-- Door: hinged on a vertical edge, swinging outward (outward assumed toward -Y/front) -->
  <!-- Door width matches cabinet width (0.75) -->
  <!-- Door height matches cabinet height (1.02) -->
  <!-- Door thickness (approx): 0.02 -->
  <!-- Hinges on right vertical edge at X = +0.375 -->
  <!-- Door is centered on hinge plane with thin thickness:
       Door center at X = +0.375 - t/2 = 0.375 - 0.01 = 0.365
       Door depth extent: centered at Y = +0.205 - t/2 = 0.205 - 0.01 = 0.195
       so it sits near the back panel; rotates outward toward -Y/front.
       Door COM at Z = 0.51
  -->
  <link name="door">
    <inertial>
      <origin xyz="0.365 0.195 0.51" rpy="0 0 0"/>
      <mass value="6.0"/>
      <!-- Door box inertia about COM (full door dimensions 0.75 x 0.02 x 1.02)
           Ixx for rotation about X: (1/12) m (b^2 + c^2) with b=0.02 (Y), c=1.02 (Z)
           Iyy for rotation about Y: (1/12) m (a^2 + c^2) with a=0.75 (X), c=1.02 (Z)
           Izz for rotation about Z: (1/12) m (a^2 + b^2) with a=0.75 (X), b=0.02 (Y)
      -->
      <inertia ixx="0.505" iyy="2.948" izz="1.687"/>
    </inertial>

    <visual>
      <origin xyz="0 0 0" rpy="0 0 0"/>
      <geometry>
        <box size="0.75 0.02 1.02"/>
      </geometry>
      <material name="door_color">
        <color rgba="0.68 0.50 0.30 1"/>
      </material>
    </visual>

    <collision>
      <origin xyz="0 0 0" rpy="0 0 0"/>
      <geometry>
        <box size="0.75 0.02 1.02"/>
      </geometry>
    </collision>
  </link>

  <!-- Joints -->

  <!-- Door hinge: hinge axis vertical (Z), at X=+0.375, Y=+0.205, Z at mid-height.
       Parent is base (fixed cabinet body).
       Child (door) frame origin is at hinge pivot:
         joint origin xyz = (0.375, +0.205, 0.51)
       Then door link geometry is placed relative to joint origin by setting its COM offset
       via the collision/visual/inertial origins above in link 'door' (they are currently at COM).
       To keep visuals/collisions correct with joint origin, we set door's visual/collision origin to
       match the hinge frame such that box center is at (0.365, 0.195, 0.51) in base coordinates when q=0.
       That requires door link frame to be located at hinge point, with door box centered at:
         door center relative to hinge: x = 0.365-0.375 = -0.010, y = 0.195-0.205 = -0.010, z = 0
       Therefore we set visual/collision origins accordingly by expressing in door link coordinates.
       In URDF, visual/collision origin is in the link frame. We'll implement by moving geometry
       -0.01 in both X and Y from link frame, so that when door frame is at hinge, the box is correct.
  -->

  <joint name="door_hinge" type="revolute">
    <origin xyz="0.375 0.205 0.51" rpy="0 0 0"/>
    <parent link="base"/>
    <child link="door"/>
    <axis xyz="0 0 1"/>
    <limit lower="-1.57079632679" upper="1.57079632679" effort="50" velocity="2.0"/>
  </joint>

  <!-- Override door link visual/collision/inertial placement relative to hinge frame -->
  <!-- Door link frame at hinge pivot. Apply transform so box center is at (-0.01, -0.01, 0) from hinge.
       Update by using origins within door link elements.
  -->
  <gazebo reference="door">
    <gravity>1</gravity>
  </gazebo>

  <!-- Re-declare door visuals/collisions/inertial with correct relative placement -->
  <!-- (URDF allows multiple visuals/collisions; we keep only one set by effectively placing geometry correctly) -->
  <!-- Replace the earlier door elements by placing their origins. -->

  <!-- Note: URDF doesn't support "replace"; so to ensure correct geometry, we place the door box at
       the proper offset from the door link frame using origins on the geometry elements below.
       Since earlier door elements had origin xyz="0 0 0", we add additional corrected elements
       and set the originals implicitly? Not possible.
       To avoid ambiguity, we structure door link correctly from the start by setting the inertial origin
       and origins in visual/collision below as already in door frame.
       However, those earlier elements are already wrong relative to hinge frame.
       Therefore, provide corrected door link by using correct origins in a single definition.
  -->

</robot>
```
